lessons.0.slides.1.title: What Is a Grand Cru?
lessons.0.slides.1.content: Grand Cru is the highest tier in the Burgundy classification system, representing the finest terroir. Burgundy has only 33 Grand Crus (excluding Chablis), totalling around 550 ha — just 2% of the entire appellation.
lessons.0.slides.2.title: 👑 Grand Cru Characteristics
lessons.0.slides.2.points.0: Label shows only the vineyard name — no village name needed
lessons.0.slides.2.points.3: Price typically 3–10× that of Premier Cru
lessons.0.slides.2.points.5: The ultimate expression of each appellation
lessons.0.slides.3.title: 📊 Grand Cru Distribution
lessons.0.slides.3.points.0: Côte de Nuits: 24 Grand Crus (23 red, 1 white)
lessons.0.slides.3.points.1: Côte de Beaune: 8 white Grand Crus + 1 red
lessons.0.slides.4.title: Grand Cru Recognition Criteria
lessons.0.slides.4.content: Grand Cru classification is based on centuries of experience and modern scientific validation: soil analysis, aspect studies, historical pricing, and consistency of quality. Once granted Grand Cru status, a vineyard keeps it permanently — the ultimate acknowledgement of terroir.

lessons.1.slides.7.content: Morey-Saint-Denis Grand Crus are seriously undervalued — priced at just 60–70% of Gevrey-Chambertin equivalents, yet matching them in quality. Clos de la Roche and Clos Saint-Denis are outstanding value investments.

lessons.2.slides.1.content: Chambolle-Musigny has only 2 exclusive Grand Crus, but both are the most elegant expressions in the Côte de Nuits. A portion of Bonnes-Mares also lies within the village.

lessons.2.slides.3.points.3: Distinction: the only Côte de Nuits Grand Cru to produce a small amount of white wine

lessons.2.slides.5.title: Clos de Vougeot
lessons.2.slides.5.content: One of Burgundy's most famous Grand Crus — and also its most controversial. At 50.6 ha, it is among the largest Grand Crus and has over 80 individual owners, resulting in wildly varying quality.

lessons.2.slides.6.points.6: Top producers: Anne Gros, Méo-Camuzet, Leroy

lessons.3.slides.8.title: Investment and Collecting
lessons.3.slides.8.content: Vosne-Romanée Grand Crus are must-haves for top collectors. Guidance: DRC wines require the highest budgets; other fine producers such as Leroy and Méo-Camuzet offer superior value; Richebourg and RSV are the most accessible entry points.

lessons.4.slides.7.title: Grand Cru Summary
lessons.4.slides.7.content: Burgundy's 33 Grand Crus represent the world's greatest Pinot Noir and Chardonnay. Each has a unique character — the ultimate expression of its terroir. Investing in Grand Cru is not merely buying fine wine; it is acquiring an irreplaceable piece of cultural heritage.

lessons.5.slides.0.description: How to taste, select, and invest in Grand Cru wines
lessons.5.slides.1.title: 🍷 Keys to Tasting Grand Cru
lessons.5.slides.1.points.1: Decanting: young reds 1–2 hours, old wines 15–30 minutes
lessons.5.slides.1.points.3: Time: observe how the wine evolves over 15–30 minutes
lessons.5.slides.1.points.4: Notes: record how aromas, palate, and finish develop
lessons.5.slides.1.points.5: Patience: young Grand Cru may need hours to fully open
lessons.5.slides.2.title: 🏆 Principles of Grand Cru Selection
lessons.5.slides.2.points.0: Producer first: the same Grand Cru varies enormously by producer
lessons.5.slides.2.points.1: Know the parcel: especially critical for large sites like Clos de Vougeot
lessons.5.slides.2.points.2: Vintage matters: great-vintage Grand Crus are the best investments
lessons.5.slides.2.points.3: Trustworthy source: ensure authenticity and correct storage
lessons.5.slides.2.points.4: Fair price: avoid hyped wines trading at irrational premiums
lessons.5.slides.2.points.5: Ageing potential: buying young means you need cellar space
lessons.5.slides.3.title: 💡 Investment Guidance
lessons.5.slides.3.points.1: Intermediate: Clos de la Roche, Musigny
lessons.5.slides.3.points.2: Top tier: Romanée-Conti, Montrachet, La Tâche
lessons.5.slides.3.points.3: Value pick: Morey-Saint-Denis Grand Crus are undervalued
lessons.5.slides.3.points.5: Hold period: at least 10–20 years to appreciate fully
lessons.5.slides.4.title: ⚠️ Common Pitfalls
lessons.5.slides.4.points.0: Fakes: especially DRC, Leroy, and other trophy names
lessons.5.slides.4.points.1: Hype-driven pricing: some vintages trade at irrational levels
lessons.5.slides.4.points.2: Poor storage: light, temperature, and humidity all cause damage
lessons.5.slides.4.points.3: Drinking too early: young Grand Cru remains closed for years
lessons.5.slides.4.points.4: Ignoring the producer: the vineyard name alone tells only half the story
lessons.5.slides.4.points.5: Following the crowd: buying names you don't understand
lessons.5.slides.5.title: The True Meaning of Grand Cru
lessons.5.slides.5.content: Grand Cru is more than expensive wine — it is the crystallisation of centuries of terroir research and a treasure of human civilisation. Every bottle of Grand Cru tells a unique story of place, one worth a lifetime of exploration and appreciation.
